title: The Water Pump — Zimbabwe (Mbira Folk)
style: Zimbabwean mbira folk urban grooves acoustic guitar hosho shakers ngoma drums warm baritone 82bpm analog tape warm storytelling Shona heritage farm memory
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The water pump sat at the edge of the lower paddock field
Between the cattle trough and the fence that wouldn't yield
You had to prime it twice before it gave up what you needed
The water pump required patience and that message had been heeded

[Chorus]
The water pump, the water pump
Standing in the red dust of the African midday
The water pump, the water pump
Everything on the farm flows through it on its way
The water pump knows the drought before we do
The water pump keeps going — that's all we ask it to

[Verse 2]
The children learned to pump it when they couldn't reach the handle
They grew into it slowly like a flame grows into candle
The sound it made was rhythmic and the farm ran on that sound
The water pump's the heartbeat of the thirty acres round

[Bridge]
Now the pump is older and the farm has changed its face
But somewhere in the family there's a muscle memory trace
Of the two-handed pull and the water rushing through
The water pump remembers even when we lose the view

[Outro]
The water pump still knows… the farm still knows… the water knows…
The gardens still growing
